extracted.intended_audience: media scholars, journalism researchers, and graduate students in communication/media studies
extracted.subtask_description: Framework for analyzing how journalists' shared narratives, touchstone cases, and discursive practices shape newsworthiness and selection. Useful for coding news stories, predicting coverage cycles, and situating professional norms as cultural narratives rather than formal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive Community
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists are bound together not by formal certification but by shared interpretations of key past events that anchor professional identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat 'professional norms' as living narratives journalists tell one another (e.g., about the Kennedy assassination, Watergate, the Vietnam draft). These shared interpretations shape what counts as legitimate journalism and thus what counts as news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Cases / Touchstones
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific historical events serve as touchstones that journalists invoke to make sense of new situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Watergate, the Pentagon Papers, the Kennedy assassination. Touchstones function as anchors; new stories are often framed by analogy to these canonical cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discursive Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories are valid (newsworthy) when they fit recognized interpretive patterns established by touchstone cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsworthiness emerges when a story 'fits' the community's recognizable narrative repertoire; discursive authority flows from conformity to those patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Touchstone Activation
rubrics_metrics.description: New stories become news partly by analogy to established touchstone cases ('the next Watergate,' 'another Pentagon Papers').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The analogical link to a touchstone confers newsworthiness and frames coverage; coding for explicit textual analogies can identify when activation occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative-Template Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Templates from past stories (e.g., the lone reformer, the cover-up, the heroic source) are applied to new stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events that map onto these narrative templates are easier to report and more likely to be selected; identify recurring templates when analyzing story selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heroic-Reporter Mythology
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that valorize investigative journalism (echoing Woodward & Bernstein) get amplified within the profession because they affirm community identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage favors narratives that present reporters or sources as heroic truth-tellers; such stories help reaffirm professional self-image and are thus privileged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discursive Boundary Maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists police what counts as 'real' journalism versus partisan, advocacy, opinion, or entertainment work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boundary disputes influence selection — pieces deemed outside the profession's definitions are excluded or marginalized. Observe language that delegitimizes alternative forms as an indicator of boundary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorial Reaffirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Anniversary coverage re-narrates touchstone cases, sustaining the interpretive community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage spikes on anniversaries (5/10/20 years) re-inscribe touchstones; these acts of memorialization maintain and circulate the community's narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Touchstone Resonance (implicit selection criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Events that map onto canonical touchstone cases receive coverage via frame inheritance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a new event resonates with a touchstone, outlets are more likely to adopt inherited frames and to follow up; coding for resonant elements predicts placement and prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heroic-Narrative Fit (implicit selection criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories admitting heroic-reporter or heroic-source narrative templates are more reportable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether stories permit a heroic framing of reporters/sources; stories enabling such narratives are preferentially pursued and amplified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional-Identity Reaffirmation (implicit selection criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that confirm journalists' self-image as truth-tellers and accountability-watchdogs are pursued enthusiastically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors stories that allow journalists to perform and reaffirm their occupational identity; look for meta-commentary that positions coverage as 'holding power to account.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-outlet Discursive Convergence (implicit selection criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Major stories generate cross-outlet interpretive convergence; deviation from the consensus interpretation is rare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After initial framing, outlets tend to converge on similar interpretations and templates; measure consensus and note when outlets resist or reframe the dominant narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award-Worthiness (implicit selection criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that align with what wins professional prizes (Pulitzers, Polks, Murrows) are pre-selected for fitting professional definitions of excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award norms influence selection: stories with investigative depth, dramatic narratives, and public impact are more likely to be treated as newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness as a Community Judgment (implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond structural news-factors (e.g., Galtung-Ruge), what counts as news depends on whether it fits the interpretive community's narrative repertoire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate cultural-narrative variables in analyses of news selection rather than relying solely on structural determinants; evaluate fit with communal repertoires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictable Coverage Cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a story gets framed via a touchstone case, subsequent stories activate the same framing, producing predictable coverage cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track the propagation of frames over time; initial touchstone activation often yields a chain of follow-ups using the same templates and metaphors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical Specificity of Touchstones
rubrics_metrics.description: Different generations' touchstones (e.g., Civil Rights, Vietnam, Watergate, 9/11, Iraq War) produce different newsworthiness patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When coding or comparing periods, account for generationally specific repertoires that shape what gets selected and how it is framed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical Bridging (methodological implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds a cultural-narrative layer above organizational and structural layers (bridging Tuchman/Gans with cultural sociology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the interpretive-community lens to complement organizational and structural approaches; integrate narrative coding with institutional analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalizability: Codeable Indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories can be coded for touchstone-case references (textual analogies to Watergate, Pentagon Papers, etc.) as predictors of placement and follow-up coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: develop codebooks that flag explicit analogies, narrative-template features (heroic reporter/source, cover-up plot), anniversary-triggered pieces, and markers of boundary rhetoric to predict prominence and endurance.
